root_cause.text: Untrusted firmware-reported frame_size values are used directly to calculate memcpy lengths without validation against the fixed 64-byte iocb member size in struct purex_item, allowing buffer overflow across structure member boundaries.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds explicit bounds checks `if (total_bytes > sizeof(item->iocb.iocb))` in both qla27xx_copy_multiple_pkt() and qla27xx_copy_fpin_pkt() functions to cap total_bytes before memcpy operations. The CVE description states that "the frame_size reported by firmware is used to calculate the copy length into item->iocb" without prior validation, and that "if the reported frame_size exceeds 64 bytes, subsequent memcpy calls will overflow the iocb member boundary." The vulnerability exists because the code trusted firmware input (le16_to_cpu(purex->frame_size)) without sanitizing it against the actual destination buffer size.
